nodes.rationale: Images built by CI and pulled from GHCR — the host never builds; Postgres lives outside the stack via shared external network.

nodes.norm_label: native dev workflow (host app + docker infra only)

nodes.label: External Postgres Dev Option
nodes.rationale: Tradeoff: no infra on laptop / shared state across machines vs offline breakage and risk of pointing migrations at prod DB.

nodes.label: Browse Daemon Model (long-lived Chromium)
nodes.rationale: AI agents interacting with a browser need sub-second latency and persistent state; per-command browser cold-starts cost 3-5 seconds per tool call and lose cookies, tabs, and login sessions between commands.

nodes.label: Bun Runtime Choice
nodes.rationale: Compiled binaries (~58MB single executable, no node_modules at runtime), native SQLite for cookie DB decryption, native TypeScript execution, and built-in Bun.serve HTTP server. The real bottleneck is always Chromium, not the CLI.

nodes.label: @ref Element Addressing System (@e/@c refs)
nodes.rationale: Playwright Locators are external to the DOM, avoiding injected data-ref attributes which break under CSP, React/Vue hydration reconciliation, and shadow DOM. Refs cleared on navigation by design: stale refs should fail loudly rather than click the wrong element.

nodes.label: SKILL.md Template System (.tmpl + placeholders)
nodes.rationale: Hand-maintained docs always drift from code; generating {{COMMAND_REFERENCE}}/{{SNAPSHOT_FLAGS}} from source metadata makes nonexistent commands unrepresentable. Committed (not runtime-generated) because Claude reads SKILL.md at load time with no build step, CI can validate freshness, and git blame works.

nodes.label: Crash Recovery (exit-and-restart)
nodes.rationale: No self-healing: when Chromium crashes the server exits immediately and the CLI starts a fresh one on next command — simpler and more reliable than reconnecting to a half-dead browser process.

nodes.label: Multi-Workspace Browser Isolation
nodes.rationale: Random port selection (10000-60000) replaced the old 9400-9409 scan that broke constantly in multi-workspace setups; each workspace gets its own Chromium process, cookies, tabs, and logs with zero configuration.

nodes.label: Auto-Upgrade Mode Proposal (GSTACK_AUTO_UPGRADE)
nodes.rationale: Power users and CI environments want zero-friction upgrades without being asked every time; deliberately deferred until user feedback confirms the prompt-based upgrade flow is stable.

nodes.label: Convert Remaining Skills to .tmpl Templates
nodes.rationale: Five non-browse skills still copy-paste the update-check preamble, so every preamble change (like the || true fix in v0.3.5) requires five manual updates; {{UPDATE_CHECK}} placeholder prevents that drift.

nodes.label: user-roles Specification
nodes.rationale: Main OpenSpec capability specification governing business user roles and route-level role protection in prata-sys.

nodes.label: Spec Purpose (TBD)
nodes.rationale: Purpose section is a TBD placeholder auto-created when archiving change phase-0-foundation-cleanup; flagged to be updated after archive.

nodes.label: Change: phase-0-foundation-cleanup
nodes.rationale: The archived OpenSpec change that originated this user-roles specification.

nodes.label: Requirement: User has a business role
nodes.rationale: Mandates every user SHALL have a role field restricted to admin, finance, or client, with scenarios covering explicit assignment, defaulting, and updates by an admin.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: user has a business role

nodes.label: role Field
nodes.rationale: The per-user role attribute holding one of three enumerated business-role values; independent of is_superuser.

nodes.label: Admin Role
nodes.rationale: Business role value and the default role; chosen as default to preserve access for existing users after migration, and admins can create/update users and their roles.

nodes.label: Finance Role
nodes.rationale: Business role value used in the explicit-role creation scenario (admin creates user with role finance).

nodes.label: Client Role
nodes.rationale: Lowest-privilege business role value; scenario shows an admin updating a user to client, and clients receive HTTP 403 on admin/finance-protected routes.

nodes.label: is_superuser Flag
nodes.rationale: Separate boolean granting unrestricted system access regardless of the business role value.

nodes.label: Role Independence from Superuser Status
nodes.rationale: Explicit design decision that the role field and is_superuser are orthogonal axes of authorization.

nodes.label: Migration Safety: Admin as Default Role
nodes.rationale: Defaulting new/unspecified users to admin intentionally preserves access for existing users after the role migration; favors availability over least privilege.
nodes.norm_label: migration safety: admin as default role

nodes.label: Requirement: Routes can require a minimum role
nodes.rationale: System SHALL provide role-based route protection via a require_role dependency, rejecting underprivileged requests with HTTP 403, including a superuser bypass scenario.
nodes.norm_label: requirement: routes can require a minimum role

nodes.label: require_role Dependency
nodes.rationale: FastAPI-style dependency mechanism that protects API routes by requiring a minimum business role.

nodes.label: HTTP 403 Forbidden Rejection
nodes.rationale: Standardized denial response returned when a user lacks the minimum role required by a protected route.

nodes.label: Superuser Bypass of Role Checks
nodes.rationale: Requests from is_superuser=true proceed through role-protected routes regardless of the user's role value.
